# x86_semantics.py cases where Rosetta and an x86 CPU differ: what it left (docs/macos/integer-data/silicon_overrides.py writes this file). One corpus line per family run on the x86 CPU, an AMD EPYC 7763 (raven-macos-bench run 44523646082, assembled with clang as here; dump sha256 8ac18705611a0e6cb61776f163b220181e59c6010fad4ed058792953cb59557c): every family, bit test the newest. The tests refuse the file when a family's cases or Rosetta's results change.
# Earlier runs gave the same results for the families they had: AMD EPYC 9V74 runs 44522174773 (random) and 44522713416 (random, multiply, divide). The random family's one difference, the RAX a 32-bit lock cmpxchg leaves, was first found on an AMD EPYC 9V45 (run 44411803673).
# Rosetta and the EPYCs agree in every register, memory byte and defined flag of the multiply, divide and bit test families; they differ only in flags x86 leaves undefined (counted by silicon_overrides.py, not written), and the bit test family not even there.

corpus	multiply	cases=1120	generated=2153868388b91462	rosetta=8329c158c8aa4e17
corpus	random	cases=10000	generated=29504b896eccb080	rosetta=70e1f67988c68548
